tagline: A forest plateau connects a railroad town with Snow Shoe.
intro: High Plateau Scenic Byway follows PA 144 through Sproul State Forest, crossing the top of the Allegheny Ridge plateau between Renovo and Snow Shoe. PennDOT records its byway designation as effective in 2002. VisitPA highlights hardwood forest, evergreens and mountain laurel, with trails and scenic vistas with parking along the corridor. The road winds through the forest and follows Hall Run near the river end.

Before the road was numbered, conservationists pressed Pennsylvania to buy land that lumber and iron companies had clear-cut. Sproul State Forest grew from that response to depleted woodland. The forest itself began with a land purchase in 1898, the first Pennsylvania made for its state forest system. PA 144 received its number in 1928. In 1935, PA 144 extended south from Carter Camp to Moshannon; paving followed in sections, including work within Sproul State Forest in 1938 and 1940.

Start at Renovo and cross the West Branch Susquehanna River into South Renovo. Traveling toward Snow Shoe reverses the highway’s winding course beside Hall Run and through State Camp. Dennison Overlook lies near State Camp. Farther south, the road becomes Ridge Road in the forest, then reaches Moshannon before turning east through Gillintown toward Snow Shoe.

moments.title: Renovo
moments.text: Renovo’s street plan has a railroad behind it. The Philadelphia & Erie Railroad built the town midway between Philadelphia and Erie, on a mostly flat floodplain beside the West Branch Susquehanna River. Its industrial grid paired avenues named for the Great Lakes with side streets numbered from 1 to 16. Incorporated in 1866, the town had houses built close together or joined in rows. The railroad shops serviced steam and diesel locomotives before closing in the 1960s. PA 144 follows Huron Avenue through town, bringing one of those lake names into the drive.

moments.title: Dennison Overlook
moments.text: Dennison Overlook, near State Camp, has a second identity as a place for astronomy. It is included in the Dark Skies Directory, at about 2,200 feet in elevation and at least ten miles from light pollution. VisitPA identifies it as a favorite site for Central PA Observers.

moments.title: Snow Shoe
moments.text: PA 144 takes the name Sycamore Street through Snow Shoe’s residential areas. A naming tradition traces Snow Shoe to a pair of snowshoes found at an Indian village near the present town site. West of the borough, the highway continues through woods, fields and development toward Gillintown and Moshannon.
